text: Your fuel distribution, down to the
Datakö brings procurement, bonded stock, sales and regulatory flows together for fuel distributors — and makes the economic performance readable day by day.
A tightly regulated business, run on estimates.

Fuel distribution follows a price schedule published every month. Between collection at the depot and the customer invoice, the value splits between customs, the Treasury, the funds and the distributor — and that split changes with the product, the sales regime and the mode of transport.
The schedule changes monthly and is tracked in spreadsheets copied by hand.
Nine sales regimes, each with its own breakdown.
What is owed and what is due gets reconstructed after the fact, operation by operation.
Bonded stock lives in the depot ledgers, the accounts live somewhere else.
The real margin on an operation only appears at closing, sometimes later.
Product, regime, volume, month. Four fields are enough: Datakö applies the SONAP schedule in force and lays out the full breakdown of the operation, line by line, beneficiary by beneficiary.
No manual calculation: this month's schedule is already in the tool.
Every component of the schedule is shown, including those at 0 GNF/L. Nothing is dropped in silence.
From procurement to the State position.
SONAP orders, proformas, bank guarantees, allocations and receipts.
Depot ledgers by product, available volumes, movements and reconciliation.
Nine regimes, customers, hauliers, invoicing and margin per operation.
Equalization, VAT collected and VAT at customs, reserve fund, gas promotion.
Economic result, operating costs, cash position and customer receivables.
Without the regulatory calculation, you reach the wrong conclusion.
Over this period the business looks loss-making until the position towards the State is accounted for. Once calculated, it is profitable. That is precisely what Distribution makes visible.
Shown on a test data set. Amounts vary from one period and one business to another.
Each role its own reading, one single source.
The real economic performance, regulatory position included.
Volumes, customers, margins per operation and per regime.
VAT, amounts due and receivables, reconciled without re-keying.
Depot ledgers, expected receipts and stock discrepancies.
